about.title: Personal Injury Help in Norwalk, California
about.longDescription: Norwalk is home to about 107,000 people, and its surface streets carry a steady load of local and cut-through traffic every day. In 2025, the city's most recent final reporting year, Norwalk recorded 413 injury collisions. Those crashes left 546 people injured and took 7 lives. Public-record counts show the heaviest volumes along Rosecrans Avenue, Imperial Highway, Pioneer Boulevard, and Studebaker Road, with reports tending to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., as the workweek lets out. Behind each of those numbers is a person dealing with pain, paperwork, and phone calls from adjusters. That is where LawProactive comes in. We are a free service, not a law firm. We do not give legal advice or handle cases ourselves. What we do is connect people hurt in Norwalk and across Los Angeles County with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain the options. There is no charge for the connection, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning you owe no fee unless there is a recovery. Whether you were hit on Imperial Highway, injured as a pedestrian near Pioneer Boulevard, or hurt on someone else's property, California gives most injury victims two years to file. Reaching out early keeps that option open.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Norwalk Claim

items.title: Two Years to Act
items.desc: California gives most injury victims two years from the date of harm to file a lawsuit. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, being partly responsible reduces your recovery by your share of blame but does not erase it. Even a driver found mostly at fault can still pursue compensation.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no legal ceiling on non-economic damages like pain, emotional distress, and loss of enjoyment of life. Your claim reflects your real experience, not an arbitrary limit.

items.title: Nothing Owed Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no upfront cost and no fee unless there is a recovery. Our connection service is free as well.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Norwalk and Los Angeles County with an independent personal injury attorney. We do not give legal advice or represent anyone. The attorney you speak with is separate from us and will evaluate your situation directly.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: Most personal injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the injury. Claims against a government entity, such as a city bus or a poorly maintained public sidewalk, can require notice within six months. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure no deadline slips by.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault. Your compensation is reduced by whatever percentage of fault is assigned to you, but you are not barred from recovering. For example, someone found 30 percent responsible could still pursue 70 percent of their damages.

items.question: What does it cost to get connected and speak with an attorney?
